evidence.quote: N. L. Anderson. He saw the New England type measure itself with another
For the first time Adams's education brought him in contact with new types and taught him their values. He saw the New England type

adjudications.reason: In the revision, 'He saw' comes directly after 'N. L. Anderson.' The source clause naming Adams was cut, so the nearest antecedent for the observer is now Anderson. Changing 'He' to 'Adams' fixes the referent at no cost in words.

evidence.quote: Speaking exactly, he got less than nothing, a result common enough in education.
chiefly because each individual appeared satisfied to stand alone

adjudications.reason: The plan marks the catalogue names as optional. The portrait still explains the disappointment through sameness: 'aggressively commonplace', and each man 'satisfied to stand alone'. The draft also keeps 'less than nothing, a result common enough in education.' The cut is a legitimate compression.

evidence.quote: but Adams had begun to fear that even in this respect one eighteenth-century type might not differ deeply from another.
yet their friendship was unbroken and even warm. Roony Lee had changed little

adjudications.reason: The plan requires that Adams 'suspected' he and Lee were equally unfit. The revision states his nearness to the eighteenth-century type as fact and drops the source's tentative 'had begun to fear'. A short restoration of that clause brings back the hedged register.

evidence.quote: The literary world then agreed that truth survived in Germany alone. The literary world had revolted against the yoke of coming capitalism

adjudications.reason: The essential point survives. 'Truth survived in Germany alone' sits directly beside the revolt against coming capitalism, and that adjacency carries the link. The explanatory clause is a reasonable tradeoff given the length budget.

evidence.quote: Adams asked the privilege, and used it to read a little, and to talk a great deal
the habit of allowing students to read with him privately in his study. As practical a New Englander as any

adjudications.reason: The essential is that reading privately in Lowell's study was the one gain. The revision describes only Lowell's habit and never shows Adams taking up the privilege, so 'pure gain' has no stated actor. Restoring the source sentence repairs this. The Harvard-influence sentence is left cut, because the slippage from fixed principles still reads clearly.

evidence.quote: to his own great astonishment, he found himself a candidate
To him the election seemed a miracle.

adjudications.reason: The draft keeps the setup for the paradox. He suffers from 'reaching his own limits', and his rival is 'undoubtedly a better orator and a more popular man'. His bewilderment is carried by 'to his own great astonishment' and 'seemed a miracle'.

evidence.quote: Self-possession indeed! If Harvard College gave nothing else, it gave calm.

adjudications.reason: The 'perfect self-possession' anecdote and 'If Harvard College gave nothing else, it gave calm' keep calm as a distinct positive gift. That already separates it from the earlier 'negative force' verdict. The echo of 'stand alone' is desirable but not necessary.

remaining_concerns: F4: the causal link between the revolt against capitalism and Germany remains implicit; restore the 'neither economical nor military' clause if the budget allows.
